MRTPC found that the producers, through their apex industry body Cement Manufacturers Association (CMA), "acted in concert" to raise prices in Jabalpur. In its order, the commission asked the manufacturers to stop and desist from such practices, while letting off another major manufacturer — Gujarat Ambuja Cement. Issuing a cease and desist order to the manufacturers found guilty of rigging prices, it has asked them "to refrain from indulging in any sort of arrangement through the instrumentality of CMA or otherwise fixing selling price of the cement in the market."

A three-member MRTPC bench, headed by chairman Justice O P Dwivedi, also directed the cement manufacturers to file affidavits of compliance of its order within eight weeks. The other cement producers pulled up include Parisim Cement, Larsen and Toubro, Satna Cement, Jaypee Cement, Diamond Cement and Maihar Cement.

The commission did not, however, find allegation of suspension of production satisfactorily proved as during the cross-examinations company officials gave different versions. Interestingly, CMA and some producers denied of any such meeting, but Larsen and Toubro admitted that such meeting was held.

On this the commission observed, "The respondents have made evasive and mutually contradictory statements regarding the meeting...conduct raises strong suspicion that in meeting some decisions were taken which they do not want to disclose."

It also noticed that there was ample evidences to show that prices in December 2000 and January 2001 was Rs 30 higher than the rates in November 2000. Rejecting CMA and producers contention, MRTPC said," cartels need not to be proved beyond reasonable doubt. According to the complaint by Cement Wholesalers Association of Jabalpur, a 50-kg bag which was sold at a price of Rs 90 in November 2000, was inflated to Rs 141 in December.

It was also alleged that on November 24, 2000, when the government under the Foreign Trade Act made Bureau of India Standard (BIS) approval mandatory for sale of cement, the producers stopped their production between November 27 to December 4, 2000, and January 12 to January 19, 2001, taking advantage of the fact that cement import could not be possible without BIS certification as importers would take some time in getting certification, they alleged.

Minutes of a CMA meeting on July 6, 2000, at Jabalpur were produced before the Commission, attended by officials of seven producers. There they decided to control the flow of cement in the market by suspending output and dispatches to dealers for five days. They had also fixed the price between Rs 107 to Rs 109. When contacted, the cement manufacturers refused to comment.

Heading: Subprime crisis ousts terrorism, West Asian conflict as gravest threat to US economy - Indian Express
Content: Microsoft still considers its takeover offer for Yahoo, currently valued at about $42 billion, to be reasonable despite Yahoo's rejection of the bid, Microsoft's chief executive Steve Ballmer said at a news conference on Monday.

Heading: Bankex slides 6.7% on farm loan waiver fears - Indian Express
Content:
The cascading fallout from the subprime loan crisis, barely a cloud on the horizon a year ago, is now viewed by experts as the gravest threat to the US economy. In a survey released today, 34 per cent of the members of the National Association for Business Economics ranked the financial market turmoil from those loan defaults as the No 1 threat to the US economy over the next two years.

That compares with 18 percent from an August survey, when the most serious threat was seen by 20 per cent of the economists as terrorism and the conflicts in the Middle East. A year ago, the credit crisis did not even register as a chief threat. The latest survey found that 18 percent of association members listed excessive debt held by households and businesses as the top problem.

The questioning of 259 economists took place during the first two weeks of February. Events since then have underscored the credit crisis problems. On Friday, the Dow Jones industrial average plunged by 315.79 points. The decline resulted from a combination of grim economic news, including a new estimate from UBS Securities analysts that the financial system losses from securities backed by mortgages and other debt would total $600 billion. That far surpassed the $400 billion that many economists projected until recently.

At the heart of financial institutions' problems are securities backed by subprime mortgages. They have gone into default at record rates because of the housing market's steep slump. These loans were extended to borrowers with weak credit histories.

A separate 49-member NABE forecasting panel recently raised its expectations of a recession, with close to half thinking a downturn will start before year's end. But 55 per cent of the forecasting panel still thinks a downturn can be avoided with the help of an $168 billion economic aid plan and aggressive interest rate cuts by the Federal Reserve.

But the policy survey highlighted the bind the Fed finds itself in. Some 10 per cent of respondents said inflation was the No 1 economic problem, a rating that put it behind worries about subprime mortgages and debt. The Fed has taken on the credit crisis and the accompanying weak economic growth by cutting interest rates. But to fight inflation, the Fed would have to raise rates. It cannot battle both threats at the same time.

In a US congressional testimony this past week, Fed chairman Ben Bernanke signaled that the central bank believes weak growth is the biggest threat at present, boosting chances of an additional rate cut when the Fed next meets, March 18.

The new NABE policy survey found that only 48 percent of those questioned believed the Fed's policies were "about right." That was the lowest reading in the past two years. It compares with 72 per cent who felt the Fed was doing a good job in the August survey, taken before the Fed started cutting interest rates.

Of those unhappy with Fed policy, 34 percent felt the central bank was lowering rates too much; some 13 percent felt it was still being too restrictive and not cutting rates fast enough. The new survey was taken after the Fed's January cuts in the federal funds rate of 1.25 percentage points, the biggest one-month reduction in a quarter-century.

Ellen Hughes-Cromwick, the president of NABE and the chief economist for Ford Motor Co., noted that the 34 per cent who believe the Fed is being too stimulative and thus raising inflation risks had more than tripled from the past survey. She said this reflected the concerns many economists have about the threat inflation poses, with crude oil prices hitting records above $102 per barrel and food costs rising.

Both consumer prices and wholesale prices jumped sharply in January. In his testimony last week, Bernanke said Fed officials were watching inflation developments closely but still believed that the slowing economy would dampen inflation in the months ahead.

On other topics, the NABE survey found only 35 percent of respondents ranked the government's budget policies as "about right," compared with 45 percent in August.

Heading: Pawar implores FM to withdraw commodity transaction tax plan - Indian Express
Content:
Leading the 900 point fall in the Sensex today were banks whose future seems uncertain post-budget 2008. In his budget speech Last Friday, finance minister P Chidambaram had announced a Rs 60,000 crore loan write-off for farmers.

The BSE Bankex was down 6.7 per cent today, losing 679 points during the day to close at 9,434.

The three biggest losers were Punjab National Bank (down 9.7 per cent), Kotak Bank (9.1 per cent) and State Bank of India (8.8 per cent).

"The correction in banking stocks is both on account of the global correction and the lack of clarity on how the farm loan waiver will be compensated," said Birla Sun Life AMC CIO A Balasubramanian. The finance minister had announced on February 29 a farm credit waiver of Rs 60,000 crore over the next three years.

"The market is not clear as to what kind of negative impact it will have on credit discipline among rural loan seekers," said the CIO of a mid-sized mutual fund house.

While the development saw investors booking profits on banking shares, the low confidence level in banking stocks is likely to continue for some time. "The market's perception will improve once clarity comes out on how the waiver will be compensated by the government," said Balasubramanian.

The fall in prices has thrown open a discount of 5-10 per cent on most of the banking stocks. The BSE Bankex is down 24 per cent since its all time high on January 14, 2008.

These are good entry levels for the long-term, considering the fact that there is nothing drastically wrong that has happened with the banking sector and they are available at good discounts, say experts.

"All falls are good, and if the fundamentals of a stock remain strong, a correction opens up opportunity to invest," said Anil Kaul, head of research with brokerage ICICIdirect.com. "A stock will continue to remain a good stock until something horrible happens."

Heading: Bihar approves investments worth $10 bn; hiccups remain - Indian Express
Content:
The Consumer Affairs Ministry has made a strong pitch for an immediate withdrawal of the commodity transaction tax (CTT) proposed in the Budget. In a missive to finance minister P Chidambaram, minister for agriculture and consumer affairs Sharad Pawar argued that the CTT would escalate transactions costs on the technology-driven national exchanges vis-a-vis the manually operated regional exchanges, the physical commodity market and the international commodities derivatives market.

The consumer affairs ministry's intervention in the matter is significant since MCX and NCDEX have opposed the proposal for the tax.

The letter, said sources, argues that the CTT would raise transaction costs by 600 per cent and drive grey market operators back to the illegal market, defeating the government's effort to bring them to the mainstream. Moreover, big corporate hedgers might move to international exchanges where transaction costs are very low.

"Thus, government's effort to create awareness among the physical market stakeholders to participate in the commodity derivatives market would get defeated by the CTT," the consumer affairs ministry said. Also, the Finance Bill, by omission, does not treat commodities derivatives transactions as business transactions vs speculative transactions as securities derivatives transactions.

According to the ministry, the commodity derivatives market and the securities derivatives market are fundamentally different in structure, characteristics and objectives. The ministry has suggested that a new clause (e) be added to the proviso in section 43(5) of the Income Tax Act to treat all commodity derivative transactions as business transactions and not as speculative transactions. This is on the same lines as has been provided under clause (d) of the same provisio in respect of the securities derivatives transactions.

Heading: Share price slide reflects world market trends: PC - Indian Express
Content:
The Bihar government has approved investment proposals worth over Rs 40,000 crore ($10 billion), including many by big corporate entities, but there are still hurdles like poor infrastructure and land acquisition, according to the state's latest economic survey. Although big firms have evinced interest in investing in the state with 115 proposals worth Rs 40,720 crore okayed by the State Investment Promotion Board, there are hiccups like land acquisition and poor infrastructure in terms of power and communication, the survey said.

Industrial sickness is another major problem as out of 26 large and medium units, 35 are closed. In the SSI sector, however, out of 72,600 units, 52,000 are functional.

According to the survey, the small scale industries are making a big contribution to Bihar's economic upsurge, apparently more than big and medium industries. Acknowledging the great role of SSIs in propping up Bihar's economic stride, the survey said, "The share of tiny industrial units among SSIs, both registered and unregistered, is as high as 99 per cent."

On the performance of large and medium-based industries vis-a-vis SSIs, it said there are only 262 large and medium units in the state with concentration only in pockets of Patna, Tirhut and Magadh divisions. SSI units, on the other hand, have a higher visibility and "small/ artisan-based industries" are spread across the state generating 5.5 lakh man-days in the current fiscal till December, it noted.

The findings indicate that the state government should give more thrust to SSI sector, providing facilities and tax sops to boost industrial production, said an expert. The survey said, although Bihar has been able to generate good revenues from litchi exports last year, the performance of agro-based units has not been impressive.

"There is, however, a big potential in agro-based industry," it added. Interestingly, unregistered units dominate the export sector in the state. Of the 1,675 export units functional, only 86 are registered.

Heading: Bajaj wants polls - Indian Express
Content:
Finance minister P Chidambaram remained unruffled by the fall in stock markets today and maintained that the downslide was only a reflection of a globalised India responding to world market trends. Speaking at the post-budget interactive session with industry chambers, he said, "Asian markets have slipped today because of fears of a recession in the US; what is happening in India shows that we are not as decoupled as we think we are."

The finance minister was replying to a query from Rahul Bajaj on today's 900.84-point fall in the Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) benchmark 30-share Sensitive Index (Sensex). "I don't think we need to worry too much about that. This is really reflecting what is happening in the world market," he added.

Expressing concern about rising food prices, he defended his budget proposal of waiving farm loans and rejected the criticism that the budget has forgotten the corporate sector. "One of the reasons why inflation is still a threat is food prices in India," Chidambaram said, adding that after a long gap India has become a marginal importer of foodgrains, which is a dangerous omen.

"Because we are dependent on imports, we are subject to world prices... No country with as large a population as India can be dependent on imports (of foodgrain)," he said. Since April 2007, the price of wheat in the global market has risen by 88 per cent and that of rice by 15 per cent, he pointed out.

"Taking all this into consideration, we came to the conclusion that farmers distress calls for an unorthodox response... the response was farm a loan waiver," the finance minister said. The wholesale price-based inflation rose to 4.89 per cent for the week ended February 16 from 4.35 per cent in the previous week.

Responding to the issues raised by the corporate sector, he said, "I have not forgotten the corporate sector. Despite the advice given by my chief economic advisor and suggestions from the Economic Survey, we accepted your (corporates') demand of retaining the peak customs duty rate."

Heading: 'Budget balances political and development needs' - Indian Express
Content: Industrialist and Rajya Sabha Member Rahul Bajaj on Monday asked the government to go in for early polls so that uncertainties could end and nation could move ahead with economic reforms. "We are tired of waiting... We want elections in 2008 so that you can come back and lead the country," Bajaj said at the post-Budget interactive session with finance minister P Chidambaram.

Heading: Is the US in recession? Yes, says Warren Buffett’s 'common sense' - Indian Express
Content:
Global rating agency Moody's Investors' Services on Monday said the Union Budget 2008-09 has tried to balance short-term political compulsions in the run up to national elections with long-term developmental needs.

"Budget 2008-09 tenuously balances short-term political imperatives with long-term developmental needs, while also trying to be consistent with key fiscal targets set forth in the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act," it said.

With the loan waiver of Rs 60,000 crore for farmers in the budget, the finance minister has focused on poor, less-educated rural dwellers. This should boost agricultural incomes in a relatively inexpensive fashion, and at a politically expedient time, Moody's said.

The budget — being the fifth and final of the Congress-led United Progressive Alliance (UPA) government — was expected to lower the fiscal and revenue deficit of the country as proposed under the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act (FRBMA) legislation.

"The budget is also particularly interesting as it marks not only the last for the UPA government, which is serving its final year, but also because it comes in the terminal year of the FRBMA," Moody's vice-president Aninda Mitra said.

FRBMA provides a legal and institutional framework to bring down the fiscal deficit and contain the growth of public debt. Remarking that the government does not make a more explicit provision for the Sixth-Pay Commission, Mitra said the budget did not address the expected hikes of public sector salaries.

"The budget does not establish a mechanism or time-frame for transferring above the line (reducing or eliminating) sizable off-budget liabilities (especially, oil and fertiliser subsidies)," Mitra said.

He highlighted that by not addressing these issues the risk on economy would rise further. "The true extent of fiscal risk is higher than nominally apparent," he added.

Although the FM, on Sunday, said buoyancy in revenue collections could meet the additional burden to pay the salary hike of Central government employees after the Sixth Pay Commission submits its report by April 4, Moody's said the continued revenue buoyancy could underpin a level of fiscal performance consistent with incremental improvements in debt ratios.

"The projected growth in the central government's budget expenditure looks extremely conservative, and this could very well be designed to make headroom for meeting additional expenses related to the Sixth Pay Commission's public sector wage recommendations," Mitra added.

Heading: Minister wants cos to steel the show, produce 300 mt a year by 2020 - Indian Express
Content:
Warren Buffett said on Monday the US economy is in recession and "stocks are not cheap." Speaking on CNBC television, Buffett also said he is no longer offering to guarantee $800 billion of municipal bonds backed by MBIA Inc, Ambac Financial Group Inc and FGIC Corp — three large bond insurers.

Buffett said that "from a common-sense standpoint right now, we're in a recession," though the US economy has not yet recorded two straight quarters of declining gross domestic product, a traditional indicator of recession.

The billionaire investor said the environment is "nothing like '73 or '74 yet," referring to a deep economic downturn also marked by rising oil prices, higher inflation and falling stocks.

Still, he said investors should not rule out a significant economic downturn, and that Federal Reserve chairman Ben Bernanke has a "very tough balancing act" in trying to boost economic growth without kindling inflation. Buffett said there is a fair chance that inflation may ignite in a "serious way."

On Friday, Buffett's insurance and investment company Berkshire Hathaway Inc reported an 18 per cent decline in fourth-quarter profit. This stemmed in part from weakness in businesses linked to housing, including units that make bricks and carpet, and that offer real estate brokerage services.

Buffett said he is finding more buying opportunities in stocks following a 16 per cent decline in the Standard & Poor's 500 stock index from its recent high in October.

"I find more things to look at now than I did six months or a year ago," Buffett said. But he acknowledged that conditions have changed "more dramatically" in the bond market. Berkshire last year spent $19.11 billion on stocks and $13.39 billion on bonds.

Falling security values and liquidity have pummeled bond insurers, which normally insure relatively safe municipal bonds but also guaranteed billions of dollars of riskier debt, often tied to subprime mortgages.

On February 12, Buffett offered to reinsure $800 billion of municipal bonds, but only at a steep premium. The offer did not include the riskier debt. Bond insurers rejected the offer and have been seeking new sources of capital or possibly breaking themselves up.

Buffett on Monday said his earlier offer was "not on the table." In December, he started his own bond insurer, Berkshire Hathaway Assurance Corp.

Since 1965, Buffett has transformed Berkshire Hathaway Inc into a $216 billion conglomerate by acquiring out-of-favour companies with strong earnings and management, and investing in stocks. Berkshire said it has 76 operating companies that sell such things as insurance, ice cream, paint and underwear.

Berkshire's Class A shares closed Friday at $140,000. Through Friday, they had risen 32 per cent in the last year.

Heading: Let FIIs enter interest rate futures mkt: RBI panel - Indian Express
Content:
Global steel heavyweights Arcelor Mittal and Posco may be finding the going tough here, but that has not deterred the Steel Ministry to maintain its optimism in increasing the sector's output in the country. Citing rising consumption levels — which is increasing at a rate of 14 per cent every year — steel minister Ramvilas Paswan on Monday increased the target for steel production for 2020 by 50 per cent to 300 million tonnes (mt).

The steel minister, in a review meeting for Greenfield and Brownfield projects with major steel producers in the country on Monday, said that there was a mismatch between consumption and production of steel in the country that needs to be addressed. "Without taking Posco and Arcelor Mittal into account, we should be producing 124 mt of steel by 2011-12 — which is slightly more than the earlier target of 110 mt. Our production right now is only 54 mt while consumption is higher at around 59 mt. We should be able to undo the mismatch by 2012 when consumption would be around 113 mt," Paswan said.

Giving the break-up of the capacity expansions that have been planned by various companies, Paswan said that steel companies have been advised to advance their plans as much as possible and not wait for the set timelines. "Steel is a basic commodity for infrastructure development and we have to keep our capex in tandem with demand. The target of 300 mt by 2020 is the minimum that has been set and we are confident that, if things work in our favour, we should actually achieve around 350 mt of production by that time," he said.

Paswan outlined five main reasons for the delay in setting up Greenfield projects including the mega-projects of Posco and Arcelor Mittal. "Problems in land acquisition, environmental issues, ports, expansion of railways and mines allocation, are some of the problems that need to be solved. We have asked the respective state governments to look into issues of mine and land allocation while we have suggested that steel makers contribute to the infrastructure development of railways, which can later be refunded from the freight costs." The minister also suggested setting up a high power committee comprising state government officials of mineral rich states — like Orissa, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh — and industry representatives to tackle the issue of allocation of mineral resources.

Officials from Posco and Arcelor Mittal, who were present in today's meeting, said they were hopeful their projects would commence this year. "There are some pending issues like forest diversion. We are working towards our April target for the start of the project," said Posco India chairman and managing director Soung Sik Cho. Posco is building a 12 mt steel plant with an estimated investment of Rs 52,000 crore —making it country's biggest FDI so far.

Arcelor Mittal India CEO Sanak Mishra said the company's two projects in Orissa and Jharkhand are progressing and construction should commence by the end of this year. "It is a close race between the projects in the two states and we are hopeful of a start by the end of this year," he said. Mittal is investing Rs 80,000 crore in the two plants that will have a combined capacity of 20 mt.

Heading: First colony for Pandits in Valley - Indian Express
Content:
A Reserve Bank expert group has proposed that foreign institutional investors (FIIs) may be allowed to take long position in the interest rate futures (IRF) market, subject to the condition that the total gross exposure in the cash and the IRF market does not exceed the extant maximum permissible cash market exposure limit which is currently $4.7 billion.

"They may also be allowed to take short position in IRF only to hedge exposure in the cash market up to the maximum permitted limit which is currently $4.7 billion. The same may also apply to NRIs participation in IRF," it said.

The panel suggested that banks be given a greater role in the interest rates futures (IRF) because restricting them to hedging will impair liquidity in the market.

"The IRF market depends, for its liquidity, depth and efficiency, on significant presence of all classes of participants.... Banks not only occupy the commanding heights of the financial sector in India but also possess the necessary technical expertise for fulfilling the role of an informed, disciplined and regulated participated class," the working group said in its report placed for public comments. It said banks should be allowed to take trading positions in IRF subject to prudential regulations including capital requirements.

To begin with, one IRF contract based on a notional, coupon bearing, 10-year GoI security be introduced in the bond futures segment. Depending upon the market response and appetite, the exchanges concerned may consider introducing contracts based on 2-year, 5-year and 30-year GoI securities or those of any other maturities or coupons, the RBI panel said.

It has recommended that the existing contract on 91-day Treasury bills futures may be retained but with settlement price based on the yield discovered at the weekly RBI auction. Besides, a contract based on an index of traded or actual call rates may also be considered.

The working group on IRF has suggested that the time limit on short selling be extended to make the maturity of the IRF instruments co-terminus with that of futures contract. It was of the view that the broader policy relating to this field should be the responsibility of the RBI while the micro details should be left to the trading exchanges.

Heading: Din in House over attacks on migrants, Govt statement today - Indian Express
Content:
Dulari Devi gingerly moves among her belongings littered outside her allotted C-1 flat on the first floor, hauls up a discoloured quilt on to her shoulder and moves in. Her family is one of the 26 non-migrant Kashmiri Pandit families, moving in the Valley's first exclusive Pandits' colony on the western outskirts of Srinagar, which would inhabit 200 families in the first phase of the J-K Government's ambitious rehabilitation package for the displaced community.

Dulari Devi lost her husband and only son in the 1997 massacre of Pandits in her Sanghrampora village. She now counts the flat among the fewer blessings from God in her tragic life. "At last, I have a place where I can die with satisfaction," Devi who did not leave Kashmir despite her tragedy, says. "I feel contended that my daughter and her children have a shelter".

The families lived in a cluster of the guarded migrant Pandit houses in Budgam town after the Government collected them from different parts of the district in the wake of the Sanghrampora massacre of seven Pandits. "We were crammed for space and four-five families lived in one house. It was a terrible life," says Bansi Lal, a retired Government employee. Lal is from Nunnar Kathwar village in Budgam. His is the only family from the 30 Pandit households of the village that did not leave Valley in the wake of the outbreak of militant violence in 1989.

However, Bansi would love to go back to his village in Kathwar if conditions improve. "I don't want to remain alienated long from our Muslim brethren," Lal says as his wife Ritu hauls belongings into her new home. "I look forward to going back to my village, sow paddy on my land and feed my livestock."

The atmosphere around the place is festive. The happy chatter of women comes from the newly inhabited rooms, the children playing around the belongings and men sipping tea on the windows. There are also the men and women from the nearby Muslim village who have come to witness the sight and talk with their new neighbours.

However, this jolly environment hides a growing unease with the trend of settling the minority community in the guarded exclusive colonies called safe zones. This is seen antithetical to Kashmir's inclusive cultural ethos of which Pandits are an integral part. Separatists like Hurriyat hawk Syed Ali Shah Geelani who recently appealed to the migrant community to return to Valley and even moderates led by Mirwaiz Umar Farooq have frowned upon the establishment of the exclusive zones for the returning Pandits. "Pandits should return and integrate back into Kashmir's life," says Geelani.

However, with Kashmir's long troubled background hanging over the current phase of marked calm in the state, authorities are in mood to take chances. The residential colony is bound by a hulking 16-feet wall topped by a steel-mesh fence with a security post on the gate. "We have no fear. But we feel the wall also is necessary," says Dulari Devi, the 10-year-old tragedy still fresh in her memory.

Heading: We’ve been cheated, say TRS MPs as they quit - Indian Express
Content:
The attacks on migrants from North India in Maharashtra led to an uproar in the Lok Sabha today with demands that Raj Thackeray, chief of the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) which is spearheading the campaign, be detained under MCOCCA and that he be disenfranchised.

As parties called for action, the ruling Congress benches remained silent. With proceedings in the House being disrupted even after two adjournments, Speaker Somnath Chatterjee directed Home Minister Shivraj Patil to make a statement on the issue tomorrow.

NDA partners accused the Congress of a entering into a nexus with the MNS but nuanced their party positions to suit their interests. The BJP was critical of the anti-North Indian campaign but did not focus on the MNS chief. The JD(U) targeted Raj Thackeray without mentioning his name.

The RJD and Samajwadi Party attacked both Raj and Shiv Sena chief Bal Thackeray, keen to see if the BJP would defend its ally. The CPM followed the Congress and BJP but launched a scathing attack on the Shiv Sena chief. As for the Shiv Sena, it distanced itself from Raj but took the line against migration into Maharashtra.

The issue was raised by Prabhunath Singh of the JD(U). He accused the Congress governments at the Centre and in the state of inaction. Raj was taken to the police station "like a bridegroom" and freed on bail within two hours of his arrest, Singh said.

Devendra Prasad Yadav of the RJD demanded that MNS be banned followed by the deletion of Raj's name from the voter list. "The nephew is trying to succeed the uncle," he said.

BJP's Shahnawaz Hussain said there was "match-fixing" between the Congress and Raj and, pointing to the treasury benches, said "you gave him full publicity."

Ramjilal Suman of the SP said Raj's campaign was on the same lines as his uncle's 40 years ago. Mohammad Salim of the CPM said, "Those who call themselves nationalists are styling themselves as Maharashtrians." "The uncle is ulcer and the nephew is just a wound," he said. "Both Congress and BJP," Salim said, "are promoting them." The Centre, he said, was only watching the "tamasha".

The House witnessed angry exchanges among Railway Minister Lalu Prasad Yadav and Salim on one side and Rajiv Ranjan Singh Lallan, Prabhunath Singh and Sena's Anant Geete on the other side.

Heading: Young turks in the house - Indian Express
Content:
Its purpose served, the Shiv Sena has decided not to make any forward move on the anti-Bihar migrant plank, at least for now.

Disclosing this here on Monday, Sena Rajya Sabha member and Saamna executive editor Sanjay Raut told The Indian Express: "We would not precipitate the matter. We would let it rest where it is, unless we come under attack from the other side."

Raut, who is known for his proximity to Sena executive president Uddhav Thackeray, said a campaign against Biharis "is not on our political agenda". "Actually, it has never been so, but we felt called upon to retaliate when some members of Parliament from Bihar like Prabhunath Singh and Devendra Prasad Yadav attacked Balasaheb (Thackeray)," he said. "A true Shiv Sainik would not take such attacks lying down and we did reply to them."

The so-called provocation from the other side apart, the Sena is no longer under pressure to match Raj Thackeray's anti-Bihari rhetoric to protect its own Marathi constituency against erosion. Raj has been forced to keep quiet following a police gag order barring him from holding rallies and addressing the media. Since no such order would last long, the competitive game has the potential to recur later. The move has already paid Raj a rich political dividend — he has been able to re-emerge from the sidelines. According to sources, MNS has managed to attract fresh recruits, causing worry to not just the Shiv Sena, but also the NCP.

As far as statements of Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar are concerned, Raut said, "We have taken them in our stride." He felt as chief minister, he has to take that position and "we understand his difficulty". However, he described him as "a competent person, who is sincerely trying to develop Bihar." Having said this, Raut registered his indignation over attempts by RJD chief Lalu Prasad Yadav and Samajwadi Party president Mulayam Singh Yadav to project certain areas of Maharashtra as pockets of people from Bihar and UP. "Who are Lalu, Mulayam, Abu Azmi and Kripa Shankar Singh to present themselves as messiahs of immigrants from UP in Mumbai? How can regional leaders of other states come and indulge in Dadagiri in Maharashtra?"

"Our message to them is leave Maharashtra to Maharashtrians and there are enough national and state parties around to take care of our state," he said.

Shiv Sena, he pointed out, had never tried to project itself as a party of Maharashtrians in states like Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Rajasthan, where Marathi-speaking people have a sizeable presence. "We have gone to other states only on the Hindutva-plank," he added.

Heading: 16 TRS legislators to resign today, but YSR sits pretty in Andhra House - Indian Express
Content:
Rajya Sabha

Jay Panda resumed Parliament after a few days of absence due to ill health. Had four unstarred questions—on a proposal to start women's universities in all states, Ultra Mega Power Project and private power plants in Orissa and the possibility of setting up adoption resource centres in states Supriya Sule had three questions—on the details of 11th Plan allocation for education, setting up of mobile courts for speedy justice, literacy mission and related problems and power shortage in Maharashtra

Kanimozhi had three unstarred questions—on student-teacher ratio in IIMs, measures to make appointment of HC/SC judges transparent, and data on children living on the streets Rajeev Chandrasekhar asked five questions: On 11th Plan targets in education, proposal to set up 100 new universities, regulation of charges levied by private schools for prospectus and application forms, the proposal to set up 10 ultra mega power plants and the running of old age homes in the country

Lok Sabha

Jyotiraditya Scindia and Rahul Gandhi were sitting together and conversing for a long time. Scindia's sole question was on India's arms deals with the US and more specifically on the purchase of Super Herculese C-130J aircraft Sachin Pilot was present in the morning session. He later went to the AICC office for some organisational meeting.

Sandeep Dikshit was seen making loud noises when it came to protesting against Leader of Opposition L K Advani's statements on the "motion of thanks". He shouted slogans when BJP leaders charged the UPA with price rise and going soft on terror Manvendra Singh sat quietly through bulk of the afternoon session. He left soon after Advani's speech Dushyant Singh has not attended the session at all so far. He is in Jaipur but there were five questions by him: on the export of milk products, on bird flu and measures taken to control it, the number of suicides reported by farmers and their state-wise details, on the National Horticulture Mission and details of the schemes cleared by the Central Water Commission in different states.

Shamik Lahiri attended the House, but had no questions Omar Abdullah continues to skip the session Naveen Jindal had three questions—on the allotments and lifting of commodities under PDS in various states, losses incurred by post offices in the country and the national food security mission Milind Deora had two questions—one on the decline of textile and handicraft exports and the other on compulsory military service Jitin Prasada was away in Madhya Pradesh attending a Congress rally Kuldip Bishnoi and Mehbooba Mufti were present; Sukhbir Badal (SAD) and Deepender Hooda were absent from the House.

Priya Dutt was not see.

Heading: BJP, CPM pressure UPA on women’s Bill - Indian Express
Content:
Stepping up their agitation for a separate Telangana state, the Telangana Rashtra Samiti (TRS) leaders seem to have gone on a resignation spree. While four of its MPs resigned on Monday, 16 of its 26 MLAs and 3 MLCs in Andhra Pradesh may submit their resignations to the Speaker on Tuesday morning. Their resignations, however, will not affect Y S Rajasekhara Reddy's Government as the Congress enjoys two-thirds majority in the 295-member Assembly.

Meanwhile, Telugu mega star Chiranjeevi's camp has dropped a strong hint about his impending launch into politics. The star's close aide and brother-in-law Allu Arvind, who also manages his film affairs, told entertainment networks that they were shaping up a party and Chiranjeevi will be launched into active politics shortly.

With thousands of workers of the Congress and the TDP waiting in the wings to join Chiranjeevi, the news of resignation of the four TRS MPs got sidelined in Hyderabad, which is one of the 10 districts in the Telangana region.

TRS spokesperson V Prakash said 16 of the 26 TRS MLAs would be tendering their resignations to Speaker K R Suresh Reddy on Tuesday. "They will seek an adjournment motion to discuss and seek a resolution on separate Telangana, which is sure to be denied following which they will all resign," Prakash said.

Though the TRS has 26 MLAs, 10 are dissidents who support the Congress and are unwilling to quit. The TRS, too, is hoping for an alliance with the Congress again to contest both the general and Assembly elections next year.

After setting a March 6 deadline for the UPA to begin the process of carving out a separate Telangana, the TRS's campaign gained momentum on January 26 when several MLAs handed over their resignation letters to K Chandrasekhar Rao at the Telangana Bhavan after the flag-hoisting ceremony. This was followed by campaigns across the Telangana region by the TRS in support of a separate state.

On February 23, nine TRS MLAs were suspended for two days when they raised slogans in the Assembly after their notice for an adjournment motion to discuss the Telangana issue was disallowed by the Speaker. For the last one week, the TRS has been holding demonstrations or road shows at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi in support of their demand.

However, political observers say the political drama in the last two months, culminating in Monday's resignations, has not invigorated the Telengana movement. In 2004, the TRS had formed an alliance with the Congress and contested the 2004 Assembly elections, winning 26 seats. The Congress held out a promise of a separate Telengana state while the TRS rode on fighting for separate statehood. While the issue remained in the limbo for four years, the TRS has stepped up its campaign again with both general and Assembly elections in 2009.

The history of TRS

Telangana Rashtra Samithi (TRS) was formed in 2000 with the agenda to carve out a separate Telangana state from Andhra Pradesh, constituting Hyderabad, Adilabad, Karimnagar, Khammam, Mahaboobnagar, Medak, Nalgonda, Nizamabad, Ranga Reddy and Warangal districts. Chandrashekhara Rao, a member of the Telugu Desam Party till 2000, formed the TRS with five Lok Sabha members.

• The party created a sensation by winning one third of Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies (MPTC) and one quarter of Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituencies (ZPTC) in the Telangana region within sixty days of its formation.

• In the 2004 Assembly elections, the TRS formed an alliance with the Congress (I) and won 26 state Assembly seats. The party also won 5 Lok Sabha seats. It joined the Governments at both state and Central level.

• In September 2006, the party withdrew its support to the UPA Government, accusing the Congress of betraying the people of Telangana over the delivery of its electoral promise to create Telangana, which was also put in the Common Minimum Program (CMP).

• In January, 2008, the party set a March 6 deadline for the UPA to begin the process of carving out a separate Telangana.

• On March 3, four TRS MPs — K Chandrasekhara Rao (Karimnagar), B Vinod Kumar (Hanamkonda, Warangal district), Ravindra Naik (Warangal) and T Madhusudhan Reddy (Adilabad) — resigned from the Lok Sabha.

Heading: Record 76 pc turnout in Meghalaya polls - Indian Express
Content:
With the Congress getting into the election mode, the BJP on Monday upped the ante on the UPA Government, launching an attack on every issue in the House — from farmers' debt-waiver package to internal security to the women's quota Bill. Coming down heavily on the Government for not making any budgetary provisions for farm loan waiver, Leader of Opposition L K Advani said in Lok Sabha that there were indications that general election, scheduled next year, could be advanced.

Maintaining that he supported loan waivers for indebted farmers, Advani wanted to know why budgetary provisions were not made for the purpose. He took the Government to task for its "failure" to table the Women's Reservation Bill and create a separate Telangana. The Leader of the Opposition also asked for the Government's statement on the status of investigation on the terror attacks that have taken place since 2004.

"We are prepared to support the Government on the women's reservation issue — whether it wants to bring in the original Bill or enact the suggestions made by the Election Commission (that political parties reserve one-third seats for women)," Advani said.

The issue was also taken up in the Rajya Sabha, with both the BJP and the CPI(M) pressuring the Government to bring the bill ensuring 33 per cent reservation to women in Parliament and state legislatures. "It is unfortunate that there was no mention of the Bill in the President's address," said BJP president Rajnath Singh while participating in the debate in Rajya Sabha on the motion of thanks to the President's address.

Sitaram Yechury said the CPI(M) was in favour of the Bill too. "We want the Government to introduce it. Let's see who are in support of it and who aren't," he added. Referring to External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee's statement on foreign policy, he said it was indicative of the Government's resolve to move ahead.

Heading: Naga movement founder’s village to vote for progress - Indian Express
Content:
A record 76 per cent turnout, the highest-ever for the state, was witnessed in the Assembly elections held in Meghalaya on Monday. Chief Electoral Officer P Naik said that the turnout is more than six per cent compared to last Assembly polls in 2003. The exact estimate of the turnout, which might go up slightly, would be known on Tuesday only, he added.

The day went off peacefully except one untoward incident in which a Congress worker was beaten to death by an NCP youth leader in Selsella in East Garo Hills district at 3.30 am.

Selsella NCP (youth wing) president Pilseng attacked Dinan Marak alias Bangbang, a Congress worker. Naik said police have arrested Pilseng and investigation is on.

In Selsella, NCP candidate Conrad Sangma, son of former Lok Sabha Speaker P A Sangma, is pitted against sitting legislator Clement Marak.

Late Sunday night, the police also arrested five United Democratic Party supporters under the Nongbah-Wahajer constituency for carrying firearms. Jaintia Hills Deputy Commissioner and Returning Officer F Kharkongor said the police intercepted a vehicle and found one of the occupants carrying a loaded gun. "All the five are in police custody now," he added.

In Chief Minister D D Lapang's constituency Nongpoh, Congress supporters assaulted UDP supporters on late Sunday night and set ablaze two vehicles. Nobody has been arrested so far.

As many as 331 candidates are in the fray for 59 Assembly seats. Election to Baghmara constituency has been rescheduled for March 22 as the Congress candidate contesting from the seat died recently.

Nearly 1,600 polling stations were set up for a total of 12,32,907 voters.

Heading: Poll managers adopt Naga ‘bastard language’ - Indian Express
Content:
"Nagas are not Indians, their territory is not part of the Indian Union. We shall uphold and defend this unique truth at all costs."

Entering the historic Khonoma village, one can't miss these words of Khrisanisa Seyie, the first president of the "Federal Government of Nagaland", inscribed on a huge rock pillar. Khonoma is also the village from where the legendary Angami Zapu Phizo built up the Naga national movement for a sovereign state, as India attained independence. It is also the village that has produced the first Naga graduate, half a dozen IAS officers, 100 state gazetted officers, 30 doctors, 20 engineers and more than 100 lecturers. Khonoma is the native village of J B Jasokie, a six-time MLA who was chief minister in the 1980s. And also that of T Sakhrie, a contemporary of Phizo, who too wants a sovereign Nagaland, but by non-violent means.

Though a section of Khonoma residents still believe that Nagaland will one day become "independent", a vast majority do come out to vote during elections. "A number of us still believe Phizo's dream will come true one day. But voting in an Indian election is equally important because we want development," said a youth.

Barely 24 km away from the state capital, it takes more than an hour to drive through the hilly road to Khonoma. Its 3,500-odd residents claim that one of the first things that this village needs is good roads. "With poor road connectivity, students are compelled to stay in rented accommodations in Kohima. Office-goers have a tough time. Women are the worst sufferers because they can't reach market with their farm produce in time," said Megobino Savino, a graduate who runs a shop here.

Things are worse for 50-year-old Guongu Meru, who is upset because the ongoing polls have put a halt to the arrival of visitors to this picturesque village. Meru is among the dozen housewives who have taken to village tourism with at least one room in their houses accommodating tourists mostly from foreign countries. The revenue generated supplements their family income. "While most tourists complain of poor road connectivity, they have stopped coming altogether because of the polls," said she, showing a cosy room with a clean toilet for which she charges Rs 200 per day.

Khonoma also has sanitation problems. "Most households do not have toilets. We have set up community toilets, but that is not enough," said Vizieu Chasie, a school teacher. "We are also awaiting better water supply," he added.

Candidates coming to seek votes, however, have been careful not to make tall promises. "I don't want to make any big promise just because I am contesting an election," said Achubu Meruno, Congress nominee. Meruno is the first candidate from Khonoma to contest an election after Shurhiu, who died in 1994 while still an MLA. His two opponents — Kiyanilie Peseyie and Asu Keyho — too have not made any promise.

But that does not mean the people here have given up hope. "Ours is the first Green Village in the country. We don't cut trees for jhum cultivation. We have declared 96 sq km of our village forests as Khonoma Nature Conservation and Tragopan Sanctuary. It is a conservation movement initiated by the villagers to protect the endangered Blythe's Tragopan. We have declared the entire village as a no smoking zone," said Zievi Meyase, a carpenter.

As one leaves the village, a huge plaque on the village arch, quoting a poem by former chief minister J B Jasokie says: "When the moon and stars/ With rare brilliance shine/ Brightening our way as we carry the crops home/ My beautiful homeland."

Heading: No system to check nicotine levels, Centre tells HC - Indian Express
Content:
Some term it a "corrupt lingua franca". Some dislike it so much that they even call it a "bastard language". But when it comes to communicating, especially with a member of another tribe, Nagamese is the language in Nagaland, a language so similar to Assamese that some people claim it to be an offshoot of it.

During elections, it is Nagamese that most parties and candidates prefer to use in order to reach out to as many people from different tribes as possible. Take, for instance, this music CD called "DAN for progress and peace" produced by the Democratic Alliance of Nagaland (DAN), whose Government was dismissed on January 3 and President's Rule was imposed in the state.

It begins with a song in Nagamese: "O Naga manu-khan/ mon khulike Congress policy jani lobi dei. UPA government ki dise?/ PR dise, PR dise/ Congress party ki dise?/ Army rule dise, army rule dise! (Observe carefully the policy of the Congress towards the state. It was the Congress and the UPA that had dismissed the DAN regime just for nothing)."

"Nagamese is not just a common language of different tribes in our state, it also virtually binds us together," asserts former Chief Minister Neiphiu Rio, whose Nagaland People's Front (NPF) is the main partner of DAN. The Congress, too, has hit back at the NPF and DAN in the same Nagamese. "Aise, Khaise, Jaise," says the Congress of the NPF, meaning "they came (to power), gobbled up (the funds by way of corruption) and are now gone!"

Nagaland has as many as 14 major tribes, and members of most tribes do not understand the mother tongue of others. "But Nagamese is a perverted form of Assamese which does not have even one word from any of the Naga tribal languages," says D Kuoli, professor at the Nagaland University, who has done research on Tenyidie, a language that binds together at least six tribes of the state.

"Tenyidie is understood and spoken by the Angmai, Chakhesang, Zeliang, Rengma, Puchori and Kheja tribes, and we are trying to develop it into a modern language so that people do not have to always use this corrupt Nagamese," he adds.

But Bhim Kanta Baruah, a professor of linguistics at Dibrugarh University in Assam, says Nagamese is a language that has grown out of the soil of Nagaland. "It has definitely grown out of the soil of Nagaland to cater to the need of common medium of communication of various tribes," says Baruah in his book Nagamese Katha-laga Niyom which is considered as a grammar book on Nagamese. "It has acquired distinct characteristics in its spirit and form and has a different vigour than Assamese," he adds.

No doubt, as one enters Nagaland, one hears the vast majority speak Nagamese, be it the rickshawpuller or the woman selling vegetables in the local market, or the taxi driver outside the railway station. For politicians, this language assumes more importance. "It cuts across language and ethnic barriers, and is most important when you seek votes," says I Imkong, veteran Congress leader who is also an aspirant for the chief minister's post in the event of the Congress attaining a majority in the elections.

Since Nagaland goes to polls on Wednesday, every political party is telling the people: "Sab manu vote dibole ahibi (all the people must come out to vote)".

Heading: Naxal threat tops agenda, says new Maharashtra DGP - Indian Express
Content:
The Centre on Monday admitted before the Delhi High Court that it had no proper system to measure the levels of nicotine and tar used in cigarettes.

The admission came during the hearing of a PIL, which had alleged that cigarette manufacturers were hardly adhering to the norms making it mandatory for them to list on the covers the exact amount of nicotine and tar used in their products.

The PIL filed by Puneet Gupta complained that the Centre was hardly making good use of a four-year-old law — Section 7 (5) of the Cigarette and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003 — to publish the list of ingredients on cigarette labels.

As a breather, the Centre submitted before a Bench headed by Justice T S Thakur that a proposal to introduce cutting-edge technology and infrastructure to conduct tests for determining nicotine and tar levels in cigarettes would be put forward in the next Five-Year Plan. "We do not have the necessary infrastructure now, but we have a proposal for it in the next Five-Year Plan," the Centre's counsel submitted.

Posting the case for July 17, the court directed the Centre to file a detailed affidavit on the technology and funds required for setting up the necessary infrastructure, even as it told Gupta to pitch in by filing his opinion on the technology available in advanced countries.

The high court on February 24, 2007, had made it compulsory for liquor bottles sold in the capital to print the ingredients on the labels.

Heading: CM coming, more clashes in Nandigram - Indian Express
Content:
Indicating the seriousness with which Maharashtra views the Naxal threat, the state's new police chief, A N Roy, said on Monday — in his first interview since taking over on March 1 — that it was one of the key issues on his agenda and that he would visit some of the worst-affected regions this week to take stock of the fight against the extremists.

Top intelligence sources have been warning about the growing Naxal threat in Maharashtra and suspect that their frontal organisations have begun spreading their tentacles in rural Thane, an industrial district barely 100 km from the country's financial capital.

"The Naxal issue is very important for us. Today, I held a meeting with officers concerned with the matter," DGP Roy told The Indian Express in the interview.

"Tomorrow, I will be visiting Nagpur and Amravati ranges to take stock of the situation there. In the next four or five days, I intend to visit all Naxalite affected areas in the state, so that after asessing the situation I come to know what is required to tackle the problem."

The comments by Roy, a former Mumbai police commissioner, come on the back of new information that Naxalites and their sympathisers are trying to infiltrate the industrial belts around Delhi, Mumbai and Pune and are trying to build urban guerrilla warfare capabilities.

Some of the information was gathered by internal security officials from a laptop seized following the arrest of a suspect in Jharkhand.

The Naxal problem has so far been restricted to a few pockets of eastern Maharashtra. Although Naxalites are officially said to be active in five districts in the region, their presence is considered notable only in two districts bordering Andhra Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.

While their movement does not have the same intensity as in the neighbouring states, authorities say they cannot relax vigil as an estimated 240 extremists are known to be present in Gadchiroli alone, one of the two worst-affected districts.

However, the threat to urban centres could change the nature of the insurgency, they admit.

Intelligence sources suspect that some frontal organisations of Naxals operate in Thane's tribal and backward taluks of Jawahar and Mokhada. These areas are densely forested and some of them are considered to be Communist strongholds.

The support for radicalism could not be termed as "full-fledged Naxal activity" and the movement is still in its "first stage", Thane SP Naval Bajaj told The IndianExpress.

"There are so many frontal organisations which are working in the area. So, I have informed my officers to talk to people personally and remove the middlemen from the picture," he said. "By this, we can understand the problems of the people. The problem is more a 'socio-economic' one at this point of time."

While the urban parts of Thane are a part of the Mumbai Metropolitan region (MMR) and get funds for development, the rural areas are largely neglected and these differences are being exploited by some radical groups, another senior officer said.

Mumbai gets its water from dams in the district, most of them located in the tribal taluks, but residents of the tribal hamlets walk miles to get potable water.

The tribal taluks have also reported malnutrition deaths along with problems like unemployment and poverty. The threat could blow up if not handled now, officers warned.

Heading: Land acquisition in Noida: farmers threaten to kidnap officials - Indian Express
Content:
A day after 12 people were injured in clashes in Nandigram, supporters of the Bhumi Ucched Protirodh Committee (BUPC) and the CPI(M) clashed with each other yet again at two different places in the trouble-torn area, leaving eight people injured. Unofficial estimates said 18 people were injured. So far, no arrests have been made in connection with the violence.

According to police, 15 BUPC supporters were injured when armed CPI(M) cadres fired bullets and threw bombs at a BUPC rally near Chowringhee Bazar in Nandigram on Monday morning. The rally was taken out in protest against the attack on BUPC supporters by the CPI(M) cadres at Satengabari on Sunday. The police said four out of the 15 injured were rushed to SSKM Hospital with bullet injuries while the rest were taken to Nandigram Block Hospital.

The police added that the Trinamool Congress-sponsored Nandigram bandh on Monday saw a series of clashes and tension prevailed in the area. Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee is scheduled to arrive in the area on Tuesday to distribute pattas to landless farmers.

Rakesh Gupta, IG of western range, claimed, "The situation is under control. We are taking adequate security measures for the CM's visit." According to police sources, on Tuesday, 700 police will man the CM's route and the venue for patta distribution— Nandigram College grounds.

Police contingents were sent to tension-hit villages after BUPC supporters started digging up a road to prevent the CPI(M) cadres from accessing BUPC-dominated areas.

BUPC leader Sheikh Sufiyan alleged that armed CPI(M) cadres, led by Mohammed Mijanoor, attacked their rally without any provocation. Four BUPC supporters — Sheikh Sahabuddin, Sheikh Suber, Sheikh Manjrul and Sheikh Sahanawaj — all residents of Hosainpur near Rajaramchowk, sustained bullet injuries. The CPI(M) cadres fled from the spot after BUPC supporters retaliated. As the news of the attack spread to neighbouring villages, BUPC supporters beat up some CPI(M) cadres at Satengabari with sharp-edged weapons. Three CPI(M) supporters were injured in the attack.

BUPC supporters gheraoed Nandigram police station alleging police inaction on Monday afternoon. A complaint was lodged against some CPI(M) cadres involved in the attack at Chowringhee Bazar. They dug up a portion of the Nandigram-Shyamsundarchowk Road near Kendamari following the attack. BUPC leaders have threatened to disrupt normal life in Nandigram if the police failed to nab those involved in the firing on Monday. "We have submitted a memorandum to the police making it clear that we would be forced to dig up all roads connecting villages with Nandigram, if the accused are not arrested within 12 hours," Sufiyan said.

Ashoke Bera, CPI(M) Midnapore (East) district committee member, however, blamed BUPC supporters for the violence.

Heading: Ministry set to regain control over ‘Incredible India’ title - Indian Express
Content:
The land acquisition process for the proposed infrastructure projects in Noida and Greater Noida seems to have run into rough weather with farmers devising new ways to extract maximum compensation from the authorities.

On Monday, a Mahapanchayat of farmers, held at Sorkha Jahibabad village of Noida, threatened to kidnap officials and stall work at the Noida Authority's office in Sector-6 if their demands was not met by them. According to the farmers, a letter listing their demands were sent to the Authority on February 25.

Attended by leaders of various political parties, the Mahapanchayat was held under the auspicious of Rashtriya Kisan Mazdoor Sangharsh Morcha, a day after two officials of the Taj Expressway Authority were held hostage by farmers in Rasauni village of Greater Noida.

The Mahapanchayat was attended by Ghanshyam Yadav of Bharatiya Janata Party, Dalbir Singh Yadav of Samajwadi Party and pradhans of close to 15 villages including Kakrala, Sarrafabad, Parthala, Behlolpur, Garhi Chaukhandi, Nagla Charandas, Baraula, and Salarpur.

The meeting also decided to call another mahapanchayat on March 8 at Jaganpur village, which will be attended by farmers from over 40 villages of Greater Noida. The meeting was held in the presence of the two officials of the Greater Noida Authority, who were taken as hostages on Sunday. However, the two were later released.

The new developments have put the officials of three authorities — Noida Authority, Taj Expressway Authority and Greater Noida Authority— in a piquant situation. Caught in the tug-of-war between the administration and the farmers, they now fear for their lives. "The process followed by the Authority is justified and legal under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, " a senior official said.

The farmers, on the other hand, are in no mood to relent. They allege that the authorities are trying to force a low compensation rate on the farmers while their demands are being ignored.

Though the Greater Noida Authority has increased the compensation from Rs 3.39 lakh to Rs 8 lakh per bigha recently, the farmers have been demanding a compensation of Rs 20 lakh per bigha. They are not only demanding an increase in the compensation, but also want the same rates to be implemented for all the land acquired since 2005.

Their other demands include: 1) Jobs for family members of the farmers in the industries built on their land. 2) Admission for their children in schools built on their land. 3) Speeding up the process of land allotment in return for the acquired land. 4) Special focus on development of the villages where land was acquired.

The rigid stand of the farmers, officials say, can delay work on the Taj Expressway and the Ganga expressway too.

Heading: UP cabinet secy post improper: Centre - Indian Express
Content:
The Tourism Ministry is all set to regain its control over the title Incredible India for a magazine it has been publishing for the past four years.

The claim of a publishing house over the ownership of that title has been rejected by the office of the Additional Commissioner of Police (Licensing) on the grounds that it had concealed vital information while getting the title registered in its name with the Registrar General of India.

The dispute over the title between the ministry and the publishing house—Durga Das Publications—which had brought out the magazine on behalf of the ministry from 2003 to 2007, has resulted in publication of the magazine being put on hold since last year.

Durga Das Publications had failed to get its three-year contract renewed last year, having lost in a bidding process to a rival publishing house. But instead of conceding defeat, it sought to restrain the Tourism Ministry from bringing out the magazine, arguing that the title 'Incredible India' was registered under its name with the RNI and, therefore, the ministry had no right to use that title.

The Tourism Ministry owns a copyright for the tagline 'Incredible India' and the magazine was just an extension of its hugely popular and successful campaign by the same name.

The matter went to the office of ACP (Licensing), which on last Friday cancelled the authorisation of Durga Das Publications to use the title 'Incredible India' on the ground that during the time of registration it had concealed the information that it would be publishing this magazine on behalf of the Ministry of Tourism.

"We have decided against claim of Durga Das Publications and the order has already been served on them," ACP (Licensing) Sundari Nanda told The Indian Express.

In between, the advice of the Law Ministry was sought and it was also of the opinion that Durga Das Publications had made a false representation before RNI and was engaged in a criminal conspiracy, which had resulted in losses to the Tourism Ministry.

The verdict of ACP (Licensing) paves the way for the Tourism Ministry to now approach the RNI and get the title registered under its name after which it can restart the publication of the magazine.

Heading: SC to examine ban on Jodhaa Akbar - Indian Express
Content:
The creation of the post of cabinet secretary in the state and giving him the status and pay scale of Rs 30,000, which is equivalent to that of the Cabinet Secretary of the Central Government, is improper and against the federal structure of the Constitution. This was stated in an affidavit filed by Additional Solicitor General Ashok Nigam on behalf of the Government of India in the Lucknow Bench of Allahabad High Court on Monday.

The affidavit was filed during the hearing of a PIL filed by Shiv Pratap Shukla, a practising lawyer of the Lucknow Bench. In the PIL, the petitioner had challenged the appointment of Shashank Shekhar Singh as cabinet secretary saying that it was an IAS cadre post and Singh was not from the cadre. Shukla had sought clarifications from the Centre and the state Government regarding his appointment and had appealed quashing of the same since it violated cadre rules and Article 312 of the Constitution.

Soon after coming to power, the Mayawati Government had brought in changes in the 1975 Transaction of Business Rules in order to bring Singh, a pilot by profession, on par with the state chief secretary. He was given the additional charge of administrative head of the Secretariat.

However, on Saturday, Mayawati announced in the Assembly that on Singh's request, she had relieved him of the additional charge of administrative head, besides stripping him of his cabinet minister status. On Sunday, the Government also reverted the 1975 Transaction Business Rules.

On Monday, the chief standing counsel, DK Upadhyay, who was representing the UP Government in this case, apprised the court of these government decisions and pleaded that the PIL was no more valid. Upadhyay said in the IAS Cadre Regulation, 1955, the post of cabinet secretary was not included. This clarifies that it is a non-cadre post. "Besides, post of secretary to the cabinet existed in the state since 1951 and state Government has all authority to create any post," he claimed.

The Bench, comprising Justice Pradeep Kant and Justice SN Shukla, has asked the UP Government to file its counter and has directed to list the case in the week commencing March 17.

Heading: After 35 yrs, she hears from him: ‘I’m not dead...’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Monday agreed to look into the legality of the ban imposed by various state governments on the Bollywood film, Jodhaa Akbar.

In a petition, UTV Software Communication Limited, producer of the film, has sought revocation of the ban imposed by the governments of UP, MP, Haryana and Uttarakhand, besides local bans imposed in various cities and towns, across the country, contending that such bans are a violation of the Fundamental Rights as enshrined in Article 19 of the Constitution.

"The right to make and exhibit movies has been recognised as part of the Fundamental Right to freedom of speech and expression as enshrined in Article 19(1) (a) and 19 (1) (g) of the Constitution," advocate Vikas Mehta, appearing for the petitioner, told a Bench headed by Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan.

He requested the court to take up the matter on an urgent basis as with each passing day the producer of the film is suffering huge losses. Acceding to his plea, the court directed that the matter be placed among "special mention cases." These cases are taken up separately and are not tagged with the routinely mentioned cases listed before court.

Heading: IPS officer gets notice for assault ‘order’ on judge - Indian Express
Content:
Around 8.30 pm local time on Monday, Kashmir Singh, who spent 35 years in Pakistani prisons, most of them on death row, on spying charges, finally stepped out of Lahore's Kot Lakhpath jail a free man.

Now 60 years old, the Indian citizen was released on the order of President Pervez Musharraf, said Javed Latif, superintendent of the prison.

"I am seeing the lights, the hustle and bustle. I feel like I'm in some other world," he told the Associated Press while being driven through Lahore. "Listen, I am laughing. I don't remember the last time I laughed like this."

Some people showered rose petals on the car carrying Singh as it drove out of the Kot Lakhpath prison. The release was beamed live by all Pakistani news channels.

Shortly after his release, Singh offered prayers at Gurdwara Dera Sahib, where

Sikh Guru Arjan Dev was martyred and which is located near the Badshahi mosque built by Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb. "I am happy to be released and thankful to Pakistan President Pervez Musharraf," he said.

Later, Singh was taken to a five-star hotel where he would spend the night before being driven to the Wagah border on Tuesday to be reunited with his family, which spent all of Monday with his photos in hand waiting for him.

Singh is scheduled to be united with his family at 11 am Tuesday. "Tell my family I am joining them tomorrow morning. I am not dead... I got a new life," he said.

A former policeman from Hoshiarpur in Punjab who became a trader in electronic goods, Singh was arrested during a business trip to Rawalpindi in 1973, said Pakistan's Minister for Human Rights Ansar Burney, who was instrumental in Singh's release. He was convicted and sentenced to death by a military court in Lahore, but the Government stayed his execution in the late 1970s and Singh's case then languished. Burney said some of the paperwork on Singh was missing.

Initially, Singh had been in touch with his family through letters, but that contact broke down 24 years ago after he was shifted repeatedly between prisons.

Singh's only communication with his family over this time was a single letter that he received from them many years ago.

Burney said in a statement that he had been looking for Singh for quite some time but had been unable to locate him because for the past few years, Singh had been known in prison by the name of Ibrahim. The minister learned of Singh's identity in December during a visit to his jail and pleaded with Musharraf to grant him clemency on humanitarian grounds. Musharraf "kindly ended his death sentence and issued orders for his release" last week, Burney said. "Getting Kashmir Singh released is like Eid for me," the minister added. "India-Pakistan ties will be strengthened by this."

Suresh Reddy, the visa counsellor from the Indian High Commission in Islamabad, went to Lahore to hand over Singh's travel documents at the jail. "Singh is in sound health. He has been following the news about his case on radio and TV and is excited at the prospect of seeing his family," Reddy said.

Burney will be travelling with Singh on Tuesday to see him reunite with his wife and children.

"My real purpose in going with him to India is that when this pair of swans meet after 35 years, I want to capture it with my own eyes," Burney said.

Heading: Mob justice in Nitish’s backyard, two killed - Indian Express
Content:
A woman IPS officer of IGP rank — whose conduct has come under the Supreme Court scanner for allegedly ordering her bodyguards to assault a Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) judge during his official visit to Ranchi last month — has been sent for psychiatric treatment to Ranchi Institute of Neuro-Psychiatry and Allied Sciences (RINPAS). The apex court on Monday issued a notice to the officer, Nirmala Amitabh Choudhary, the Centre, and the Jharkhand Government in connection with the attack on Justice B V Rao.

Addressing the media on February 18, Choudhary had alleged that Ralph Barleta, Bipin Chandra Dutt and Kiranmai Dutt of a Hyderabad-based BPO were involved in cyber crime and had underworld links. And when certain people connected to the underworld and based in Jharkhand came to know that she wanted to probe into their crime, she was threatened with dire consequences. "On February 15, I approached my senior colleagues for security," said Choudhary, IG (Vigilance) of Jharkhand State Electricity Board.

She wrote to Ranchi SSP that her official residence was unsafe and she should be lodged at Jharkhand Armed Police's (JAP) guest house. When she checked in at the guest house on February 21 and inquired about all those who were staying there, she was told that Rao, a CAT judge from Andhra Pradesh, was already staying there. Immediately, Choudhary barged into Rao's room and called him a terrorist from Andhra Pradesh. Minutes later, her armed guards started throwing out Rao's belongings, recalled a JAP constable, on condition of anonymity.

In the evening, an FIR was lodged by CAT's Section Officer, Bandi Bhagat, at the Doranda police station. Next day, local newspapers carried front page stories of the IG 'insulting' the judge. In protest, lawyers associated with CAT boycotted work on February 22. Eight securitymen who had accompanied her were subsequently suspended. The Patna High Court took suo motu cognizance of the case and served notices to Choudhary and her bodyguards.

On Monday, a Bench — comprising Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan and Justice R V Raveendran — treated a letter, received by the court in connection with the incident, as a writ petition and sought details from the Centre and the state about the incident.

After the incident, a police officer had said Choudhary's behaviour was not normal. She was sent to RINPAS for a check-up. The doctors at RINPAS have requested for more time for conducting a thorough examination of Choudhary, said DIG R K Mullick. RINPAS Superintendent A K Nag declined to comment on Choudhary's mental health.

Heading: NGOs against ‘consensus’ route to panchayat seats - Indian Express
Content:
Madness of mob justice in Bihar came to the fore again, claiming three lives, including two in Chief Minister Nitish Kumar's backyard Bakhtiarpur of Patna district.

Mohammad Aslam and Mohammad Azhar, in their 30s, were first beaten up and then shot dead by villagers of Teka Bigha, just 4 km away from Kumar's native house in Bakhtiarpur town, on Monday afternoon. Both the youths from adjoining Chakdaulat village were caught by angry people as they tried to flee, riding a motorcycle after killing a local, Umashankar Yadav. A third accomplice managed to flee.

"Police reinforcements have come and patrolling has been intensified," said Patna SP (rural) U K Sinha. The two youths were no habitual criminals. They were on the way to inspect crops in their fields near Teka Bigha, a Hindu-dominated village.

Aslam was carrying a licensed revolver of his father Mohammad Kalam. On the way they entered into a heated exchange with a local shopkeeper, Umashankar Yadav, with whom they had an old land dispute, police said.

When the fight reached a flashpoint, Aslam fished out the licensed revolver and fired at Yadav, killing him on the spot. As they tried to flee riding a motorcycle, villagers caught hold of the two while their third accomplice escaped.

"The mob first hit them, snatched their revolver and shot them dead. Police reached the spot after everything was over," said a local. SP (rural) U K Sinha said though the motorcycle had been recovered, the licensed revolver was still missing. A case had been registered.

In another incident, a man was lynched by villagers in Munger district of north Bihar after he shot dead a boy in a drunken state on Sunday night. Chaitanya Soren, 40, resorted to random firing from his country-made pistol on Sunday evening at Shyampur Santhali village under Kharagpur police station. One bullet hit five-year-old Babulal playing in a nearby field, killing him on the spot. Angry villagers then got together, caught hold of Chaitanya and began dispensing instant justice, killing him on the spot. Munger SP Shalin said an FIR had been lodged against unknown villagers.

On March 23, a lynch mob had pulled out a murder accused out of the hospital at Hajipur in Vaishali district and killed him.

Rajapakar in Vaishali had hit the headlines in November last year when 10 suspected thieves were lynched by villagers.

Heading: Deshmukh on edge again as Sonia summons - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the state Government has ensured that 30 per cent of the villages got their representatives elected through consensus (samras) in the recently concluded panchayat elections, the initiative has drawn flak from a section of activists who termed the process as a 'subversion of democracy.'

In the elections held on January 20, nearly 426 villages opted for 'samras', out of a total 1,436. They elected the sarpanch as well as other representatives through consensus, instead of using the ballot box.

Though the samras scheme had been in practice in the state since 1991-92, even during the time of Congress, it became popular when Chief Minister Narendra Modi increased the monetary incentives for the village panchayats during the elections held in 2001.

With increased money, the percentage of samras panchayats naturally registered an increase. According to officials of the State Election Commission, the percentage of samras villages which was hardly four to five per cent previously, jumped to 27.2 per cent in 2001 and to 30 per cent in January 2008 elections. The idea of samras, officials say, is to promote harmony, and reduce social and caste tension generated during the village panchayat elections. State's panchayati raj ministry, soon after the notification of January 2008 elections, had announced a monetary assistance of Rs one lakh for small villages having seven panchayat members and Rs 2 lakh for big villages with more than seven members. The monetary assistance, according to officials, is given to samras panchayats for carrying out developmental projects in their area.
